editorial:
Ever wondered what happens in those giant parking garages when the boss isn't looking? You get a wild ride with a group of parking lot attendants who are way too bored for their own good. These guys aren't your typical employees; they are zany, loud, and always looking for a way to make a quick buck or pull a prank. The whole vibe feels like a chaotic party where everything that can go wrong does, and the chemistry between the crew makes the madness feel real. It is a lighthearted trip back to the early eighties that doesn't take itself too seriously.

What really works here is the fast timing and the goofy energy of the cast. While some of the jokes feel a bit dated, the physical comedy still lands well. If you like movies where regular people get into over-their-heads situations, you will love this. It is a great pick for a lazy Sunday afternoon. You can currently rent it on Apple TV or look for a digital copy on Prime Video to see it in high quality. If you are a fan of old-school comedies, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move for a rainy day.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the crew's biggest scheme almost gets them fired. In the final scenes, the chaos peaks as they try to hide their tracks from the management. Luckily, a huge misunderstanding saves them, and the boss ends up thinking they were actually helping the business. They keep their jobs but learn that being honest is too boring. They wrap things up by planning an even bigger prank for the next week.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves goofy 80s comedies and workplace antics.
